1947, February 21
M. Marie Baxter. 3793 Virginie Perk Detroit, Michigan.
Any one who has been raised a Catholic, - nay who has believed in God and has fallen away from such faith, little as it may have been, will have a fearful responsibility to answer for if satisfied to meet - to take the chance of meeting - the divine King of the Banquet without having on the "wedding garment" of charity; viz, without faith, because without faith neither hope nor charity (profitable for eternity), can exist. A real and outstanding "trace of the Holy Trinity" as the divine "stamp of Heaven on the immortal soul", God will require on the Day of Judgement if we are to be admitted as having on "The Wedding-garment". Its up to the individual to preserve, to acquire, to appreciate that free gift of God's gratuituous liberality.
If God made every rational creature primarily to know Him in order to love Him and serve Him as only rational creatures can, then surely there must be something in the very nature of every rational creature inclining him to seek such knowledge. .... Therefore: "Woe to that man who through his own fault loses the faith he has once received - or who having come to the use of reason will have failed to acquire and foster it. Hoping that this may help some one in some way to wake up before too late, I beg to remain
Sincerely Yours in Christ, Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap. Praised be Jesus!
